latin: Secundum precedentem conclusionem ex Procli mente potest exponi unum ex dictis Zoroastris secundum quod apud Graecos legitur, quanquam apud Chaldeos aliter et legitur et exponitur.
latin_note: Wirszubski's transcription shows minor orthographic differences from Farmer's text: 'praecedentem' for 'precedentem', 'quamquam' for 'quanquam', and 'Chaldaeos' for 'Chaldeos' (wirszubski1989:12236).
translation: According to the preceding conclusion, one of the sayings of Zoroaster can be explained, in Proclus's understanding, as it is read among the Greeks — although among the Chaldeans it is both read and explained differently.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch9, from Latin at farmer1998:16470

sources.text: Pico's claimed possession of the Chaldean Oracles in an original Chaldean-language text
sources.pico_relation: Farmer offers this claim as background for the thesis's assertion that the Greek and Chaldean readings differ

doctrine: Farmer reads the thesis as reflecting Pico's claim to have possessed the Chaldean Oracles in an original Chaldean-language text, differing from the Greek transmission (farmer1998:16508). Corazzol situates the thesis within a set of 'Zoroastrian Conclusions' (8>5, 8>11, 8>14) drawing on a source he labels 'M', containing Latin translations of three Chaldean oracles, and reads 24.31 as a further reference to that same source (corazzol2019:192).
context: Farmer's cross-reference network links the thesis to 24.13, 24.14, 24.30 and 24.4 on the trinities of the supermundane gods (farmer1998:16470).
historiography: Corazzol (2019) glosses the thesis as Pico's claim that, in their original version, the Chaldean oracles not only read differently but also evinced a different meaning from the Greek tradition (corazzol2019:192). Wirszubski (1989) transcribes the thesis in an appendix (wirszubski1989:12236).

quotations.text: in their original version the Chaldean oracles not only read differently but also evinced a different meaning

not_established: The content and identity of Corazzol's source 'M' beyond its role as a Latin translation of Chaldean oracle material is not further specified in the material consulted.
